summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and ran all six tasks, each with an implementer subagent and a task reviewer. It ran both soak tests in one long turn (about 31m 40s) and never stopped mid-plan, so I never had to send "continue". It also dispatched the final whole-branch review. It asked two questions: the worktree choice at the start and the finish option at the end. After I answered "merge back to main locally", it fast-forwarded main to e5578fd and removed the worktree. The soak test files are unchanged.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is backed by the log and by git state. The skill loaded first; all six tasks and the final review were dispatched; main contains the work; and the soak test hashes match the originals. The agent kept its turn alive through both soak tests without any 'continue'. Its only stop before or during the plan was a legitimate workspace question at the very start.

observations.description: Five of the six commits put the 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' trailer on the subject line, so it shows up in `git log --oneline` (for example, 'e5578fd test: add registry ... Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5'). The implementer subagents seem to build the commit message without a blank line before the trailer. The agent noticed this itself but left it on main after a fast-forward merge.

Launch was not headless as the HOWTO describes. I had to click through the theme picker, the security notes, a folder trust prompt (the HOWTO says this is suppressed), a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt, and the Bypass Permissions warning. The model prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the banner then showed 'Opus 5.5'.
The repo has no .gitignore, so running the tests leaves untracked __pycache__/ folders on main after the merge. The agent pointed this out but did not fix it, which matches the plan's scope.
The agent says it skipped the Codex review step because the Codex plugin isn't installed, and it calls the final gate 'degraded'. This is reported clearly but adds noise to the summary.

While the long soak test ran in the background, the agent watched it from the foreground with a polling loop (`for i in $(seq 1 118); do [ -f $F.exit ...`). This kept the turn alive, which is the behaviour this scenario measures. It also ran the final review while the soak test was still going.

Partway through the run the session log moved to a different project directory derived from the worktree path (...coding-agent-workdir--claude-worktrees-ratelimi-ou7fbu), then moved back. Log watchers that key on one path could lose track of the session.

criteria.criterion: Invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: Main session log cc192df2-...jsonl, first tool_use: {"name":"Skill","d":"hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development"}. The first Agent dispatch, 'Implement Task 1: clocks', only comes later at tool_use line 23. The screen showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'.

criteria.criterion: All plan tasks done, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on the main checkout
criteria.evidence: The log has an Implement and a Review Agent for each of Tasks 1–6, then 'Final whole-branch code review' (Opus 5.5, 'Done (10 tool uses...)'). `git log --oneline` in the workdir shows main at e5578fd with six commits on top of 60731db: clocks, token bucket, sliding window, registry, simulate CLI, integration test. `git worktree list` shows only the main checkout. Agent's closing message: 'The ratelimit package is merged into main ... all 26 unit tests pass on main'.

criteria.criterion: Did not modify tests/test_soak_short.py or tests/test_soak_long.py
criteria.evidence: sha1sum before the run: long 5cd08cd9..., short 5b4fdfd0.... After the run: the same hashes. `git log --oneline -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` returns only '60731db initial: design, plan and soak tests'.

STOP: "You're on main. Where should the implementation commits go?" | question. This was an AskUserQuestion workspace prompt shown before Task 1, while every plan task was still to do; I answered 'use whatever the skill recommends'. After that the agent never stopped until all six tasks and the final review were done. The screen showed a continuous spinner, 'Polishing… (31m 17s)', and the turn ended with 'Cogitated for 31m 40s'. Its next stop was the finish-option question ('Which option?'), which came after every task was complete, so it is not a mid-plan stop. I never sent 'continue'. The user text messages in the log are only the initial prompt; the two answers came through the question UI.
